title: Give each CRUD verb its own RBAC action; never substitute write for create
answers: Why does a custom role with notebooks:create still not see the New notebook button?
Why can a write-only role open the create notebook dialog but the save fails?
Custom RBAC role loses notebook UI access after upgrade
Notebook create permission check uses the wrong action
body: Symptom: a custom RBAC role granted only the create action for a resource sees no create affordance (or a write-only role sees one that then fails on save). Root cause: frontend permission helpers collapsed create checks onto the write action (public/app/features/notebook/permissions.ts:canCreateNotebooks, public/app/routes/routes.tsx NOTEBOOK_NEW_URL route, public/app/features/notebook/mutation-api/commands/permissions.ts:requiresNotebookCreate all previously checked *Write instead of *Create). Fix pattern: define one action per verb that mirrors what the backend apiserver actually authorizes (pkg/registry/apis/folders/sub_access.go:160-165), and check the exact matching action for each operation — read for viewing, write for editing an existing resource, create for the creation route/action, delete for removal. Fixed built-in roles happen to bundle several actions together so this bug is invisible until a custom role grants them separately. Constraints: applies whenever a resource exposes distinct create/read/write/delete apiserver actions; does not apply if the backend genuinely authorizes create and write with the same single action.
applies: Frontend RBAC permission checks for any resource with separate create/read/write/delete apiserver actions (notebooks, and by extension similar resource types)
says: New notebook button missing when only create permission granted
Create dialog opens but save fails without write permission
Custom roles stop showing notebook interface after system upgrade
Create notebook uses incorrect permission check
search: Each CRUD verb must have its own RBAC action; never substitute write for create: check read for viewing, write for editing, create for creation routes, delete for removal, exactly matching what the backend apiserver authorizes (pkg/registry/apis/folders/sub_access.go:160-165). Fixed in public/app/features/notebook/permissions.ts:canCreateNotebooks, public/app/routes/routes.tsx:NOTEBOOK_NEW_URL, and public/app/features/notebook/mutation-api/commands/permissions.ts:requiresNotebookCreate. Constraint: applies only when backend has separate create/read/write/delete actions; custom roles that grant actions separately expose the bug. Task kind: frontend RBAC permission checks for resources with distinct apiserver CRUD actions (notebooks and similar types).
